title: Mezhgorye - The Secret City Under The Mountain

target.note: short declaratives, one idea per beat. Little to no pause between sentences.

narration:
Beneath this mountain lies a secret city.
No outsider has ever reached the tunnels.
This is Mezhgorye, in Russia's Far East.
It sits above Magadan, in frozen hills.
The winters here are brutal, and long.
Stalin ordered it built in the 1930s.
The design came from Soviet engineers.
Gulag prisoners did most of the digging.
North Korean workers were brought in too.
They cut the rock with hand drills.
Many of the workers never left the mountain.
The dead were buried inside the rock.
The tunnels run for a hundred kilometres.
Some accounts say a hundred and twenty.
Wide chambers branch off on both sides.
Power, water, and housing were all underground.
Above ground, they raised a stone fortress.
Thick walls, narrow slits, no doors out.
The only way in was by rail.
A narrow gauge line ran deep inward.
No road ever reached the front gate.
Then the country decided to forget it.
The site was formally closed, on paper.
Rumours spread of a nuclear bunker down there.
Others say a refuge for the leadership.
No document has ever confirmed any of it.
The stone fortress still stands above it.
Snow buries that gate for months.
The tunnels are still down there, unchanged.
And no outsider has ever gone in.

beats.line: Beneath this mountain lies a secret city.
beats.visual: black mountain filling the frame, snow on the rock, one sealed archway at its base; character small at the bottom edge, awed, looking up

beats.line: No outsider has ever reached the tunnels.
beats.visual: close on the archway, a solid steel door, no handle on this side; character flat-mouthed, hand on the rock

beats.line: This is Mezhgorye, in Russia's Far East.
beats.visual: hand-lettered 'MEZHGORYE' stamped across the sky over the ridgeline

beats.line: It sits above Magadan, in frozen hills.
beats.visual: wide frozen valley, low hills, a thin river; label 'MAGADAN REGION'

beats.line: The winters here are brutal, and long.
beats.visual: the same valley under deep snow, wind lines across it, character small and hunched, shivering

beats.line: Stalin ordered it built in the 1930s.
beats.visual: flat grey blueprint sheet on a table, a mountain drawn in section, label '1930s'

beats.line: The design came from Soviet engineers.
beats.visual: the blueprint filling the frame, tunnels sketched in thin pencil, a small stamped signature block

beats.line: Gulag prisoners did most of the digging.
beats.visual: line of prisoner figures in caps, hunched, carrying a drill, filling the width of the frame

beats.line: North Korean workers were brought in too.
beats.visual: a second line of figures, different coats, standing behind the first; character watching from the side, uneasy

beats.line: They cut the rock with hand drills.
beats.visual: close on hands and a hand drill against a rock face, dust falling

beats.line: Many of the workers never left the mountain.
beats.visual: empty snowdrift where figures stood, a single coat on a stake, no footprints leading away

beats.line: The dead were buried inside the rock.
beats.visual: a plain box in the rock, lids shut, no names on them; character standing small beside it

beats.line: The tunnels run for a hundred kilometres.
beats.visual: mountain in cutaway, tunnel network bored deep into the rock, filling the frame

beats.line: Some accounts say a hundred and twenty.
beats.visual: same cutaway, a hand-drawn ruler line along the tunnel labelled '120 km', the number huge

beats.line: Wide chambers branch off on both sides.
beats.visual: wide chambers branching left and right off the main bore, each with a single door

beats.line: Power, water, and housing were all underground.
beats.visual: three small icons side by side under the rock: a coil, a tank, a bunk bed; character pointing at them

beats.line: Above ground, they raised a stone fortress.
beats.visual: the stone fortress above ground on its ridge, thick walls, tiny slit windows, filling the frame

beats.line: Thick walls, narrow slits, no doors out.
beats.visual: close on a slit window, arrows of cold wind passing through it; the outer wall has no opening

beats.line: The only way in was by rail.
beats.visual: narrow gauge rail line running from the bottom of the frame into a tunnel mouth; character riding on it, small

beats.line: A narrow gauge line ran deep inward.
beats.visual: the same rail line from the side, rails narrowing into the dark, no other line anywhere

beats.line: No road ever reached the front gate.
beats.visual: a road drawn on the surface above, ending abruptly at a cliff edge; label 'NO ROAD'

beats.line: Then the country decided to forget it.
beats.visual: the drawn road and label fading out to blank paper, character shrugging at the empty page

beats.line: The site was formally closed, on paper.
beats.visual: an official stamp slammed onto the page, the word 'CLOSED' under it, red ink

beats.line: Rumours spread of a nuclear bunker down there.
beats.visual: rumour scrawled on the wall in the tunnel, a rough mushroom cloud, half crossed out

beats.line: Others say a refuge for the leadership.
beats.visual: a row of drawn empty chairs underground around a long table, no one in them; character awed

beats.line: No document has ever confirmed any of it.
beats.visual: character shrugging, both palms up, flat-mouthed; speech bubble 'nothing on paper'

beats.line: The stone fortress still stands above it.
beats.visual: the stone fortress on the ridge, seen from far below, small against the rock; label 'STILL STANDING'

beats.line: Snow buries that gate for months.
beats.visual: the same ridge in deep winter, drifts over the gate, only the top wall showing

beats.line: The tunnels are still down there, unchanged.
beats.visual: cutaway again, the long dark tunnel, unchanged, a lamp far down it; character small at the mouth

beats.line: And no outsider has ever gone in.
beats.visual: the steel door from the opening, filling the frame, shut; character facing it from the snow, still
